day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary Airport at 14:00. Take the Banff Airporter shuttle (~$60 CAD one-way, book in advance for best rates) to Banff town (~1.5 hours). Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge. Pick up a free Banff National Park trail map at the Banff Visitor Centre on Banff Avenue — it's a 5-minute walk from most lodges. Stroll Banff Avenue to get oriented, grab groceries at Nesters Market for budget breakfasts and snacks for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely walk to Bow River Falls (free, 15-minute walk from downtown) to shake off travel fatigue and catch the golden-hour light on the Rockies. Easy, flat, and beautiful after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during your flight.
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or snacks at the Calgary Airport or bring food from home for the shuttle ride.
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro on Banff Avenue — affordable vegetarian-friendly bowls and wraps (~$15–$20 CAD). Alternatively, pick up groceries at Nesters Market and cook a simple meal if your lodge has kitchen access.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Parks Canada Discovery Pass on arrival if you haven't already (~$75 CAD/person for an annual pass — it pays for itself within 2–3 days and covers all park entry fees). Keep Day 1 light; jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Stock up on trail snacks (granola bars, nuts, fruit) at Nesters Market to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike — depart by 8:00 AM to beat the crowds. Drive or take the Roam Transit Bus Route 8X (~$6 CAD each way) to Johnston Canyon, about 25 km west of Banff. Hike the iconic canyon trail through carved limestone walls to the Lower Falls (1.1 km one-way) and continue to the Upper Falls (2.7 km one-way). The catwalk boardwalks bolted into the canyon walls are spectacular. Allow 2.5–3 hours total for both falls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue past the Upper Falls on the trail to the Ink Pots — seven cold-water springs with vivid blue-green pools (~5.8 km one-way from the trailhead, moderate difficulty). This extends the hike into a rewarding half-day adventure through open meadows with mountain views. Return to Banff by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax with a soak at Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$20 CAD entry) — perfect for tired hiking legs. The outdoor mineral pool sits at 1,585 m with panoramic mountain views. Afterward, walk along the Bow River trail at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at the lodge using groceries from Nesters Market (oatmeal, fruit, yogurt — budget ~$3–5 CAD).
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch from the lodge: sandwiches, trail mix, fruit, and a refillable water bottle. There is no food available at Johnston Canyon trailhead.
meals.dinner: Tooloulou's on Bear Street — generous portions of Cajun-inspired comfort food at reasonable prices (~$18–$25 CAD). Try their wraps or pasta dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Start early — Johnston Canyon is one of Banff's most popular trails and parking fills by 9:00 AM. Roam Transit is the most budget-friendly option. Wear layers; the canyon is cool and shaded even on warm days. Bring a light rain jacket just in case. The Ink Pots extension adds ~4 km round-trip but is highly recommended for those who want a fuller day.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake & Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek — this is the most time-sensitive day of the trip. Moraine Lake Road requires a Parks Canada reservation or you must take the Moraine Lake shuttle from the Lake Louise Park & Ride. Book the Parks Canada shuttle in advance (~$8 CAD each way). Depart Banff by 6:30 AM. Begin with the Rockpile Trail (short, 15-minute scramble) for the iconic panoramic view of Moraine Lake and the Valley of the Ten Peaks — one of the most photographed scenes in Canada.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Moraine Lake Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km round-trip, easy) along the vivid turquoise shoreline. Then tackle the Consolation Lakes Trail (5.8 km round-trip, moderate) for a quieter, rewarding extension through boulder fields to two serene alpine lakes with dramatic cliff backdrops. Return shuttle to Lake Louise Park & Ride and back to Banff.
day_by_day.evening: Grab a cold drink and relax on the patio at Banff Ave Brewing Co. — local craft beers on tap and pub food at mid-range prices. Watch the sunset paint the mountains from the rooftop-style patio.

meals.breakfast: Early self-prepared breakfast at the lodge before 6:30 AM departure (overnight oats or instant oatmeal, banana, coffee from a thermos).
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — bring extra food and water as there are no budget food options at Moraine Lake. The lodge café there is expensive.
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. — burgers, nachos, and pub mains around $18–$24 CAD. Happy hour deals available on drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake access is highly restricted in summer 2027 — book the Parks Canada shuttle weeks in advance. Do NOT attempt to drive Moraine Lake Road without a reservation; you will be turned away. Arrive at the Lake Louise Park & Ride at least 20 minutes before your shuttle time. Bring bear spray (rentable in Banff for ~$10/day) for the Consolation Lakes trail. This is the most iconic day of the trip — prioritize it.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike — take the Roam Transit Route 8X to Lake Louise (~$6 CAD each way) or join a shared shuttle. Arrive early (by 8:00 AM) to enjoy the famous turquoise lake before crowds build. Walk the Lake Louise Lakeshore Trail (4 km round-trip, easy) with stunning views of the Victoria Glacier. Then begin the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail (14 km round-trip from the lake, moderate) — one of Banff's finest hikes through moraines and glacial terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail to the historic teahouse (open mid-June to mid-October, cash only). Treat yourself to a tea or hot chocolate at the teahouse (~$5–$8 CAD) — a true Banff tradition. The views of the glaciers and surrounding peaks from this elevation are extraordinary. Descend back to Lake Louise and catch the shuttle back to Banff.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Bow Falls and the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel exterior (free) — stroll the grounds and enjoy the fairy-tale castle views at golden hour. This is a great low-cost evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at the lodge. Pack an extra-large trail lunch today — it's a long hike day.
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch on the trail. Budget for a tea or snack at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (cash only — bring bills).
meals.dinner: Melissa's Missteak on Lynx Street — a Banff institution since 1972. Hearty portions of burgers, pasta, and Canadian comfort food at reasonable prices (~$18–$26 CAD). Great atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: The Plain of Six Glaciers full hike is ~14 km round-trip with ~365 m elevation gain — allow 5–6 hours. Wear sturdy hiking shoes. Bring trekking poles if you have them for the rocky upper section. The teahouse is cash only — bring $10–$15 CAD in bills. Lake Louise can be extremely crowded on summer Saturdays; early arrival is essential. The Roam Transit bus is the easiest and cheapest way to get there.

day_by_day.morning: Tunnel Mountain Trail — a perfect, accessible hike right from Banff townsite. The trailhead is a short walk from the lodge. Hike to the summit of Tunnel Mountain (4.8 km round-trip, easy-moderate, ~260 m elevation gain) for sweeping 360-degree views of the Bow Valley, Banff townsite, and surrounding peaks. Allow 1.5–2 hours. A great morning hike that requires no transportation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Vermilion Lakes — walk or rent a bike (~$15/hour at Banff's local bike shops) along the Vermilion Lakes Drive (~9 km round-trip from downtown). Three shallow lakes with stunning reflections of Mount Rundle. Exceptional wildlife spotting area — look for elk, beavers, ospreys, and herons. Free and easily accessible. Stop at the Banff Visitor Centre to learn about the park's geology and wildlife at their free interpretive displays.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening to explore Banff townsite. Browse the shops on Banff Avenue, visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (small entry fee ~$10 CAD, free on certain evenings), or simply sit by the Bow River and enjoy the mountain scenery.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at the lodge — this is a good morning to use up any remaining groceries.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget-friendly meal at The Hungry Squirrel on Banff Avenue — smoothies, wraps, and healthy bowls at very reasonable prices (~$12–$16 CAD).
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the lodge using groceries, OR splurge slightly at Coyotes Southwestern Grill on Caribou Street — flavourful Tex-Mex and southwestern dishes, good value for Banff (~$18–$24 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Day 5 is intentionally lighter to rest legs before the final full day. Tunnel Mountain is excellent for sunrise if you're an early riser — the light on the Rockies is magical. Vermilion Lakes at sunset is one of the most photographed spots in Banff — consider revisiting in the evening for golden-hour photography. Bike rentals are a fun and affordable way to explore the lakes area.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at Two Jack Lake — take a short drive or taxi (~15 min from Banff) to Two Jack Lake for a peaceful, crowd-free morning. The lake offers stunning reflections of Mount Rundle at sunrise. Walk the easy lakeshore path (free with Parks Pass). Then head to Johnson Lake (nearby, also free) — a smaller, warmer lake perfect for a refreshing swim on a warm summer morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the C-Level Cirque Trail (~8.6 km round-trip, moderate, ~455 m elevation gain) starting from the Upper Bankhead parking area near Lake Minnewanka. This underrated trail passes through ghost-town ruins of an old coal mine before opening to an alpine cirque with wildflowers and dramatic limestone walls — far fewer crowds than the main park trails. Return to Banff and begin packing for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Banff — walk the Bow River Loop trail at sunset one last time. Pick up any souvenirs on Banff Avenue (look for budget options like postcards or locally made items). Enjoy a farewell dinner and reflect on the week.

meals.breakfast: Pack a sunrise picnic breakfast to enjoy at Two Jack Lake — thermos of coffee, muffins or pastries from a bakery the night before.
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch for the C-Level Cirque hike.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Bear Street Tavern — wood-fired pizzas and casual atmosphere, great value for Banff (~$18–$22 CAD for a pizza). Perfect relaxed final night.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure logistics on Day 6 evening — if flying home on Day 7, book the Banff Airporter shuttle in advance (departs Banff multiple times daily toward Calgary Airport, ~$60 CAD). Two Jack Lake and Johnson Lake are free with your Parks Pass and rarely crowded in the morning — a serene way to end the trip. C-Level Cirque is a hidden gem that most tourists skip; highly recommended for a rewarding final hike. Ensure bear spray is returned if rented.

day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary International Airport at 14:00. Collect luggage and take the Banff Airporter shuttle (~1.5 hrs) to Banff town. Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along Banff Avenue to get oriented. Stop at a Parks Canada Visitor Centre to purchase your Banff National Park Entry Pass (Discovery Pass) – essential for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Explore downtown Banff on foot. Walk across the Bow River Bridge and enjoy views of Mount Rundle at golden hour. Head to dinner and then wind down with a casual walk along the riverside trail near the hotel.

meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or wrap at the airport before boarding or en route
meals.dinner: The Bison Restaurant & Terrace – mid-range, locally sourced Canadian cuisine with a cozy mountain atmosphere. Budget ~$35–50 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Nothing is scheduled before 14:00 arrival. Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm shuttle booking in advance; Banff Airporter runs regularly from YYC. Pick up trail maps and park info at the Visitor Centre while purchasing your pass.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike – Set out early (depart hotel by 8:30 AM) to beat the crowds. Drive or take the Roam Transit bus (~30 min) to Johnston Canyon trailhead. Follow the dramatic carved limestone canyon trail to the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and continue to the Upper Falls (2.7 km one way). The catwalk boardwalks hugging the canyon walls are stunning. Allow 2.5–3 hours round trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff town by early afternoon. Enjoy lunch, then spend the afternoon visiting the Banff Gondola & Sulphur Mountain Summit. Ride the gondola to 2,281 metres for sweeping 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges. Walk the Ridgeline Interpretive Boardwalk at the summit (~1 km loop) and visit the restored Sanson's Peak Meteorological Station. Allow 2–2.5 hours total.
day_by_day.evening: Descend back to town and relax. Browse the Banff Avenue shops or visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (open until 5 PM). Enjoy a well-earned dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or Whitebark Café – great coffee and pastries, budget ~$12–18 CAD
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from Nesters Market (grab supplies the night before or morning of) enjoyed near Johnston Canyon parking area
meals.dinner: Saltlik Steakhouse – mid-range steaks and Canadian comfort food, ~$40–55 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon gets very busy by 10 AM in July – an early start is strongly recommended. Roam Transit Route 8X serves the Bow Valley Parkway including Johnston Canyon; check current schedules. Gondola tickets should be booked online in advance to secure your preferred time slot and avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake & Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek – This is the crown jewel of the trip. Moraine Lake Road is reservation-only by Parks Canada shuttle in peak season; book your shuttle ticket well in advance from Banff or Lake Louise. Depart by 7:00–7:30 AM. Hike the Rockpile Trail first (short, 300 m) for the iconic Valley of the Ten Peaks panorama – one of the most photographed views in Canada. Then tackle the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return) along the impossibly blue glacial lake. Allow 3–4 hours of hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Lake Louise village for lunch. Browse the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise grounds, then begin the Lake Louise Shoreline Hike – walk the iconic turquoise lakeshore and, if energy allows, continue up the Plain of Six Glaciers trail toward the historic teahouse (~5.5 km one way from the lake). Even hiking partway offers breathtaking glacier and mountain views. Return to the lakeshore by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff (45 min drive or shuttle). Rest, shower, and enjoy a relaxed dinner. Consider an evening walk along the Bow River or Vermilion Lakes Road for potential wildlife spotting (elk, beavers, waterfowl).

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel – pack energy bars and trail snacks for the morning
meals.lunch: Laggan's Mountain Bakery in Lake Louise Village – famous sandwiches, soups, and baked goods; budget ~$15–20 CAD
meals.dinner: Tooloulou's Restaurant in Banff – Cajun-Canadian fusion, lively atmosphere, mid-range pricing ~$30–45 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake access is strictly managed in July 2027 – book Parks Canada shuttle tickets as early as possible (they sell out months ahead). Bring layers; mornings at Moraine Lake can be cool even in July. This is the most activity-heavy day; wear well-broken-in hiking boots and carry at least 2L of water per person.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and Recovery Morning – After two big hiking days, take a slower start. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, then take a gentle walk around the Banff townsite. Visit the Cave and Basin National Historic Site (a short walk or bike ride from downtown) – the birthplace of Canada's national park system, with interpretive exhibits and thermal spring pools. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a canoe or kayak on the Bow River or Lake Minnewanka (20 min drive from Banff). Lake Minnewanka is the largest lake in Banff National Park and offers stunning mountain-framed paddling. Alternatively, join a guided lake cruise on Minnewanka for a relaxed 1-hour narrated boat tour. Return by mid-afternoon and explore the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a soak (~$20 CAD entry) – a perfect way to soothe hiking muscles.
day_by_day.evening: Casual evening in Banff town. Visit a local craft brewery or enjoy a cocktail on a patio. Stroll Banff Avenue as the evening light hits the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Coyotes Southwestern Grill – popular Banff breakfast spot with hearty options, ~$18–25 CAD
meals.lunch: Picnic at Lake Minnewanka with supplies from a local deli or Nesters Market
meals.dinner: Bear Street Tavern – wood-fired pizza and craft beer in a relaxed setting, ~$25–35 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: This is an intentionally lighter day to prevent burnout midway through the trip. The Banff Upper Hot Springs are open daily in summer; arriving around 4–5 PM avoids the peak afternoon rush. Canoe and kayak rentals at Lake Minnewanka are available through local outfitters – book ahead on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive – One of the world's most spectacular drives. Depart Banff by 8:00 AM and drive north on Highway 93 toward Jasper. Key stops include: Bow Lake and Num-Ti-Jah Lodge viewpoint, Peyto Lake Viewpoint (short 800 m walk to a stunning wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake), and Mistaya Canyon (short 900 m trail to a dramatic limestone canyon). Drive at a leisurely pace, stopping frequently for photos and short walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Columbia Icefield area (~2.5 hrs from Banff). Stop at the Athabasca Glacier viewpoint and walk the Toe of the Glacier Trail (free, 1.5 km return) for an up-close look at the ancient glacier. Visit the Glacier Discovery Centre for exhibits on glaciology and climate. Begin the return drive south along the Parkway, watching for wildlife (bears, mountain goats, bighorn sheep, elk are commonly spotted). Arrive back in Banff by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Banff. Visit Vermilion Lakes at sunset – just minutes from downtown – for golden-hour reflections of Mount Rundle in the still water. This is one of the best photography spots in the Canadian Rockies.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab-and-go from a local café
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial picnic lunch to enjoy at Peyto Lake or Bow Lake – no restaurants along this stretch
meals.dinner: Maple Leaf Grill & Lounge – upscale-casual Canadian cuisine, great for a special evening, ~$45–60 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Fill up your gas tank before leaving Banff – there are very few services along the Icefields Parkway. Carry bear spray (rentable in Banff) when doing any trail walks. The Athabasca Glacier Ice Explorer tours (motorized ice vehicle rides onto the glacier) are available but expensive (~$65–80 CAD); they are optional and can be skipped for budget reasons. Start early to have maximum time and avoid afternoon tour-bus crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning Hike – Tunnel Mountain Trail, Banff's most accessible summit hike, departing right from the townsite. A steady 2.3 km ascent (one way) through Douglas fir forest leads to a summit at 1,692 m with sweeping views over the Bow Valley, Banff town, and surrounding peaks. Allow 1.5–2 hours return. Perfect for a final morning in the mountains without needing a car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town, pack up, and check out of Banff Mountain Lodge. Grab a final lunch in Banff. Depart for Calgary International Airport via the Banff Airporter shuttle (book your return seat in advance). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the drive and airport check-in. Enjoy one last look at the Rockies as you leave the park.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary or overnight in Calgary if flight is the following day.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel before checkout – fuel up for the hike
meals.lunch: Eddie Burger + Bar – beloved local Banff spot for gourmet burgers and poutine, ~$20–28 CAD; a great final Banff meal
meals.dinner: Airport dining or Calgary restaurant if departing late

day_by_day.notes: Tunnel Mountain Trail is dog-friendly and family-friendly – a wonderful low-key finale to the trip. Check out time is typically 11 AM; ask the hotel if you can store luggage while you do the morning hike. Confirm your Banff Airporter return shuttle timing based on your flight schedule. Return your Parks Canada Discovery Pass – it is valid for the full calendar year so keep it if you plan any other Canadian national park visits in 2027.

meals.dinner: The Maple Leaf Restaurant — Banff Avenue; reserve the elk tenderloin or cedar-planked salmon with a local craft cocktail or fine Canadian VQA wine

meals.dinner: Eden Restaurant at Rimrock Resort Hotel — book the Chef's Tasting Menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings for a truly luxurious evening

day_by_day.notes: Book Banff Gondola tickets online in advance to secure your preferred morning time slot. Wear sturdy hiking shoes for Johnston Canyon — the catwalk can be slippery near the falls. Johnston Canyon is approximately 20 minutes west of Banff town by car.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (07:00) for Moraine Lake — arrive before 08:00 as private vehicles require a shuttle reservation or very early arrival due to access restrictions. Hike the Rockpile Trail (short but iconic — 300 metres) for the world-famous Valley of the Ten Peaks viewpoint, then continue on the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km loop) along the breathtaking turquoise shoreline. The vivid glacially-fed blue of Moraine Lake is most vibrant in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes to Lake Louise for the Lake Louise Shoreline Hike. Walk the flat, scenic lakeshore trail and continue up the challenging but rewarding Plain of Six Glaciers Trail to the historic teahouse at 2,135 metres (11 km return, ~4 hours). Enjoy tea and homemade baked goods at the teahouse with glacier views.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Fairview Bar & Restaurant inside the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise — an iconic lakeside dining experience with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the lake at dusk. Indulge in Alberta prime rib or pan-seared trout in an elegant heritage setting.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the lodge before 06:30 departure — request the lodge prepare a grab-and-go breakfast bag the night before
meals.lunch: Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse — enjoy freshly baked scones, soups, and hot drinks with one of the most spectacular alpine views in Canada
meals.dinner: Fairview Bar & Restaurant, Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise — reserve a window table for lake views during the golden hour

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake road access is strictly managed in summer 2027 — pre-book the Parks Canada shuttle from Lake Louise Ski Resort or the Lake Louise Park & Ride well in advance. Carry bear spray (available to rent in Banff) for both hikes. The Plain of Six Glaciers trail gains 365 metres in elevation — trekking poles recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated nature and wildlife morning along the Icefields Parkway — one of the world's most scenic drives. Depart by 08:00 and drive north along Highway 93. Stop at Bow Lake for a short lakeside walk and stunning reflections of Crowfoot Glacier. Continue to the Crowfoot Glacier viewpoint and Peyto Lake Lookout (a short 800m walk to one of the most photographed views in Canada — a wolf-shaped turquoise lake).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the Columbia Icefield area. Book a premium Ice Explorer glacier tour onto the Athabasca Glacier with Pursuit (Brewster). Walk on a 10,000-year-old glacier with a knowledgeable guide and visit the glass-floored Glacier Skywalk suspended 280 metres above the Sunwapta Valley. Begin the scenic return drive to Banff in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the lodge. Enjoy the on-site spa facilities — book a hot stone massage or alpine herbal treatment to soothe hiking muscles. Casual dinner at Bison Restaurant & Terrace in Banff town for rustic-chic mountain cuisine featuring bison, wild game, and locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Columbia Icefield Glacier Discovery Centre restaurant, or pack a premium lunch from the lodge for a scenic roadside picnic at Bow Lake
meals.dinner: Bison Restaurant & Terrace — try the bison short rib or wild boar charcuterie board with a glass of BC Okanagan red wine

day_by_day.notes: The Icefields Parkway round trip to Columbia Icefield is approximately 4 hours of driving total. Pre-book the Ice Explorer and Skywalk combo tickets online — they sell out quickly in peak summer. Bring sunscreen and sunglasses as glacier UV exposure is intense. Fill up with gas in Banff before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike on the Tunnel Mountain Trail — a moderate 4.8 km loop departing just minutes from Banff town centre. Summit at 1,692 metres for panoramic views of the Bow Valley, Banff town, and surrounding peaks. A perfect, accessible morning hike with big rewards. Return to the lodge for a leisurely late breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the natural hot springs and wellness culture of Banff. Visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a soak in the historic mineral pool with mountain views (the highest commercially operated hot springs in Canada). Then spend the afternoon exploring the Banff townsite in depth — visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for art and history, browse high-end outfitters and galleries along Banff and Bear Street.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell-style dinner at Saltlik Steakhouse — Banff's premier steakhouse serving AAA Alberta beef with an impressive wine cellar. Order the bone-in ribeye or prime tomahawk steak. After dinner, join a guided evening wildlife safari by private 4x4 vehicle along the Bow Valley Parkway to spot elk, deer, bears, and wolves in the golden evening light.

meals.breakfast: Post-hike brunch at the lodge or at Tooloulou's — known for indulgent eggs Benedict, French toast, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Picnic supplies from Nourish Bistro or Banff Ave Brewing Co. patio for casual lunch with craft beer and mountain views
meals.dinner: Saltlik Steakhouse — reserve the prime tomahawk for two and pair with a Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon from their curated cellar

day_by_day.notes: The guided evening wildlife safari (book through the lodge concierge with Discover Banff Tours or Banff Adventures) typically runs 3 hours from 18:00–21:00 — schedule dinner before or after accordingly. Bring binoculars for wildlife viewing. The Tunnel Mountain hike is dog-friendly if travelling with pets.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for a peaceful sunrise canoe on the Bow River or Vermilion Lakes. Rent premium canoes through the lodge or a local outfitter. Paddle among wetlands with views of Mount Rundle reflecting on the still water — a magical, serene Banff farewell. Return by 09:30 for a full breakfast and check-out preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge. Depending on return flight timing, enjoy a final scenic drive along the Bow Valley Parkway (Highway 1A) — a quieter, wildlife-rich alternative to the Trans-Canada — stopping at Castle Mountain viewpoint and Johnston Canyon one last time if desired. Private luxury transfer departs Banff for Calgary International Airport (allow 2 hours for the drive plus airport check-in time).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Calgary International Airport. If the flight is late evening, enjoy a final meal at the Calgary Airport's Chop Steakhouse & Bar in the departure terminal, or pre-clear time at the Plaza Premium Lounge for a comfortable send-off.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge — order the full Canadian breakfast with eggs, back bacon, and fresh-baked pastries
meals.lunch: Picnic or roadside stop along Bow Valley Parkway, or a quick stop at Baker Creek Bistro near Lake Louise for gourmet sandwiches and coffee
meals.dinner: Calgary Airport or en route depending on flight schedule — Chop Steakhouse & Bar (Departures level, YYC) for a satisfying final Alberta beef meal

day_by_day.notes: Schedule check-out by 11:00 and confirm private transfer timing with the lodge the night before. Return all rented gear (bear spray, trekking poles) before departure. Consider purchasing Parks Canada National Park souvenir passes or local artisan gifts from Banff Ave shops on the final morning. Keep a light layer accessible in carry-on — Calgary airport can be cool even in summer.

query: Banff hiking and lakes, $2800 couple, 6 days, July 2027, from Calgary
